invariant: Java computes a flat state diagram's SVEK body envelope by drawing the same clusters, nodes, and solved edges used for final output through LimitFinder. The union includes each primitive's painter semantics: UEmpty contributes its complete rectangle; URectangle starts one pixel above and left and ends one pixel inside plus shadow; UEllipse ends one pixel inside plus shadow; ULine contributes both endpoints; DotPath contributes every cubic endpoint and control point after shaft retraction; UPolygon contributes polygon extrema plus ten horizontal pixels on each side; and UText contributes its measured box from baseline-height+1.5 through baseline+1.5. SvekResult then translates every node, edge, and cluster by (6-minX, 6-minY) and reports the painted span plus 15 pixels. At the file boundary, CucaDiagram.getDefaultMargins adds its backward-compatible 5-pixel right and bottom margins. SvgGraphics.ensureVisible then integerizes that final positive dimension exactly once as (int)(dimension+1), equivalent to ceil(dimension) except that an already integral dimension gains one. Rust must therefore apply Java's integerization to painted-span-plus-20, not add one to the floating dimension and ceil it again. The minimum visible painter sits at coordinate 6. Arrowhead polygons remain at the unretracted contact tip while the shaft is shortened by the decoration length, and the complete solved label block participates in the same envelope. Width, height, and origin are therefore one consequence of the emitted primitives and named export decorators, not independent Graphviz layout dimensions or node-rank heuristics.
causal_divergence: The Rust flat state path reconstructs the envelope in several disconnected passes. Its minimum x pass unions state boxes, note origins, and unretracted spline points but omits arrowhead polygons and complete label boxes. Its y origin comes from svek_origin_y_for_layout and the top node rank, so an up/right spline that rises above every node cannot move the body down. Its maximum pass separately considers node extents and spline points, conditionally substitutes LayoutResult.width/height for labeled graphs, and only computes selected label maxima. This mixes Graphviz's layout envelope with Java's painted envelope and has no single source of truth for primitive minima, decoration overscan, retracted paths, or UEmpty label bounds. The resulting fractional translations and canvas changes across state_complete_2, state_complete_3, state_only_initial_final, state_labeled_initial_transitions, state_arrows_up_right, state_fork_join_with_labels, state_end_pseudostate, state_ends_1, and state_ends_3 are consequences of missing painters, not fixture-specific offsets. state_labeled_final_transitions is explicitly excluded: its canvas and nodes already match while two same-endpoint routes are exchanged, which is a separate transition-to-layout-edge identity mechanism.
planned_change: Build one primitive-aware painted-bounds collector from the solved flat state scope and the exact data used by final emission. Feed it state and note painters, retracted routed paths, arrowhead vertices with LimitFinder polygon overscan, full solved label and link-note boxes, and any title-independent SVEK painters. Derive graph_body_x and graph_body_y solely from 6-min, derive the SVEK result from painted span plus 15, add the named Cuca right/bottom margin, and integerize once with SvgGraphics.ensureVisible's (int)(dimension+1) rule. Reuse the same route/decorations and text metrics as emission so bounds cannot drift from output. Remove result.width/result.height and top-rank origin heuristics from no-oracle SVEK body sizing once the collector covers their painters. Preserve oracle mode and document-title composition outside the SVEK body. Do not encode fixture offsets, branch-count ladders, direction-specific canvas constants, or coordinate-keyed SVG rewrites.
